value.body: Hospitality graduates work in flight kitchens that prepare airline meals, in airline guest-service roles, and in food, beverage and housekeeping departments on cruise ships. Flight catering is production work on tight schedules and strict food-safety rules; cruise work means living on board for months at a stretch.

items.label: Cruise contracts
items.note: Followed by unpaid leave; length varies by line and role

items.label: Cruise prerequisites
items.value: STCW basic safety training + seafarer document
items.note: Indian crew usually need a CDC from DG Shipping

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A BHM or hospitality diploma, with some hotel or kitchen experience. Flight kitchens and airlines hire directly; cruise lines hire through their own recruitment or licensed manning agencies, followed by interviews, a medical, safety training and visa formalities. Check that any recruiting agency is licensed with DG Shipping.

value.title: At a glance
items: Cruise work can mean long days, seven-day weeks and months away from home.
Food-safety, hygiene and timing standards in flight kitchens are strict.
Experience at sea or in a flight kitchen carries over to hotel and institutional catering roles.
